title: fix(desktop): skip turn lease for bare-profile primary routes
claim: retainGatewayForSessionTurn must not register a turn lease for a bare-profile route (connectionId null, profile == primary) that rides the primary socket, because nothing ever releases it.

evidence.red: NOT RED on main. A probe (fork's own tests plus a temporary _turnLeaseKeysForTests helper, not committed) in apps/desktop/src/store/session-request-router.test.ts passes 3/3: bare-profile primary (legacy) registers no lease; bare-profile primary with primaryConnectionId='local' registers no lease; bare non-primary 'loki' still registers ['loki\u0000sess-loki'].
evidence.negative_control: Removing main's `if (!g.secondaries.has(scope)) { releaseRoute(); return () => undefined }` guard (from e1374093aa) makes both bare-primary probe tests fail, so the probe is sensitive and main's guard is what fixes it.
evidence.adjacent: Main already has gateway-connection-lifecycle.test.ts 'lets the next turn take a real hold after a turn that rode the primary socket'.
evidence.source: main apps/desktop/src/store/gateway.ts retainGatewayForSessionTurn (L1689+) returns a no-op and stores no key when g.secondaries lacks the scope, which covers every primary-socket route, including the bare-profile primary.

upstream_overlap: Fixed by e1374093aa (John Paul Soliva / jonpol01) 'fix(desktop): never register a turn lease that nothing can release', landed via #114986 (MERGED, teknium1 salvage of #113798) for issue #113795 (CLOSED).
notes: Retire the fork leaf. Main's outcome-based guard is more general than the fork's shape-based guard. Kanban baggage ignored.
